intent: Harden the post-Baseline governance guardrails discovered by independent architecture audit and add a bounded multi-Agent workstream control plane without reopening Architecture Baseline v1 semantics. Fix frozen-tag migration validation, bind Change Contracts to their live capability-admission intent, require concrete L3 architecture evidence/approval before protected semantic changes, and provide per-workstream branch/cursor/path ownership so concurrent industry/product Agents can extend existing semantic owners without sharing one mutable global cursor.
rationale_summary: Baseline v1 is healthy, but the guard implementation still has three control-plane gaps: schema_through is incorrectly tied to current HEAD migrations, stale L3 Change Contracts are not intent-bound, and protected changes do not machine-require reviewed L3 evidence. Concurrent Agents would also fight over global current.json/admission/contract files. Extend existing governance/continuity owners with narrow validators and per-workstream cursors rather than creating another semantic-owner system.
